# bugs #4233: (unsigned char)(nh << 1) passed to a wider parameter arrives as 0x0100

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4233/
- Category: [Analyzed, not fixed](../../unresolved.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Review the ticket's patch for its effect on code size. Add the ticket's program as a test, with objects that are not static.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176 the program in the ticket passes 0x0100 to `sink` for `(unsigned char)(nh << 1)`. The
value must be 0. For mcs51 the program was linked with a `sink` that stores its argument, and it
was run in ucsim. `sink` receives 0x0100 in the small model, in the small model with
`--stack-auto`, and in the medium model. It receives 0 in the large model, with and without
`--stack-auto`. With `static` in the declaration of `nh`, it receives 0 in the small model. For
z80 and stm8 the program was compiled and not run. Their assembly shifts 16 bits and sign-extends
the result to 64 bits. pic16, where the reporter found the problem, was not built.

More arguments were run for mcs51 in the small model. These arrive with a wrong value:

- `(typeof (nh))(nh << 1)` and `(unsigned char)(nh + nh)` arrive as 0x0100.
- `(signed char)(sh << 2)` arrives as 0x0100 when the `signed char` object `sh` is 0x40.
- `(unsigned char)~nv` arrives as 0xffffffffffffffff, and `(unsigned char)-nh` arrives as
  0xffffffffffffff80.
- `(unsigned char)(nh << 1)` arrives as 0x0100 when the parameter is `unsigned long` or
  `unsigned int`.
- `(unsigned char)(nh << 1) == 0` arrives as 0, and the correct value is 1.

These arrive with the correct value: `(volatile unsigned char)(nh << 1)`, the shift of a `volatile`
object, `(unsigned char)(nh * 2)`, `(unsigned char)(nh << 1) + 1ull`,
`(unsigned long long)(unsigned char)(nh << 1)`, and an `unsigned long long` object after the
assignment of `(unsigned char)(nh << 1)`.

## Known

The cause that the ticket describes agrees with the code of r17176. `processParms` in
`src/SDCCast.c` calls `decorateType` for the argument. For the operand of the cast, `decorateType`
uses the result type `char`, and `computeType` returns a copy of the type of `nh` as the type of
the shift. `compareTypeExact` finds this type equal to the type of the cast, and `decorateType`
returns the shift node without the `CAST` node.

The argument then has the type `unsigned char` and needs a conversion to the type of the
parameter. `processParms` copies the argument with `copyAst`, makes the copy the operand of an
implicit `CAST` node, and calls `decorateType` for that node. `copyAst` does not copy the
`decorated` flag. `decorateType` therefore computes the type of the shift again, now with the
result type of the parameter, and the shift becomes an `int` operation.

`compareTypeExact` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` also compares the `static` flag, the storage class, and the
qualifiers of the two types. The copy that `computeType` returns has the `static` flag and the
storage class of `nh`, and `allocGlobal` sets the storage class of `nh` to `xdata` in the large
model. In these cases, and for the `volatile` cast, `compareTypeExact` finds a difference and the
`CAST` node stays.

## Open

The patch in the ticket removes the cast only when its operand is a value node. It was not applied
or tested here. With it, `CAST` nodes stay in the tree for every other operand in every context,
so the code size of the regression tests and of the libraries must be compared before and after.

A regression test must declare its objects without `static`. It shows the defect only in the
models that do not place those objects in `xdata`. A test with `static` objects passes on r17176.

## Related

The cast removal in `decorateType` is also the cause of bugs #3674 and #3172. The fork has a patch
for them in `processParms`. With the fork's patches the program of this ticket still passes
0x0100 in the small model. By the code, the patch in this ticket keeps the `CAST` node for the
operands of those two tickets as well. The two patches were not tested together.
